independent.summary: `brief()` bounds caller-supplied values to 60 chars but does not strip CR/LF, so a client can forge log lines in the deploy console (e.g. `response_type=x%0A[oauth:light] GET /authorize serving the Allow page...`) — the values printed at light (`response_type`, `code_challenge_method`, `grant_type`, `client_id`) are all attacker-controlled and newlines pass through unescaped.

The new pending-code ceiling is global and `POST /authorize` has no rate limit, so any registered user (registration is open) can issue 500 approvals in a burst and make every other user's connector authorization fail with 503 for up to five minutes, repeatable indefinitely — an availability regression the unbounded map did not have; a per-user cap would bound the same memory without the cross-tenant denial.

`createHash('sha256').update(code_verifier)` still throws when `code_verifier` is absent or arrives as an array from a repeated parameter, so such a request becomes a 500 INTERNAL from the error handler instead of the `invalid_grant` refusal — the same malformed-input class the change hardened one line earlier for `code` (`typeof code === 'string'`) and that the fingerprint helper's comment says must 'reach its refusal line rather than throw'.

grades.reason: Describes the pre-change code: the merged `POST /oauth/token` no longer logs `req.body`, and line 133 is now the discovery document's `authorization_endpoint`.
The `[...authCodes.keys()]` dump is gone — the miss line now prints only the fingerprint and `authCodes.size` (oauth.js:282) — and line 148 is now the `response_type` check.
The unbounded map is exactly what this change fixes: `sweepExpiredCodes()` runs on every issue and `maxPendingCodes()` caps the map with a 503 (oauth.js:116, 228-237).
The 'computed vs stored' challenge line was removed entirely; the mismatch refusal at oauth.js:296 names the rule and prints neither challenge.

triageGrades.reason: The change edits the OAuth authorize/token handlers, including a new 503 refusal path ahead of the identity write.
The whole change is about keeping codes, verifiers and challenges — credentials redeemable for MCP_BEARER_TOKEN — out of the log.
No billing, pricing or AI-budget code is touched.

Nothing persisted is deleted or overwritten; the only new deletions are already-expired in-memory map entries that were invalid anyway, and the cited line 25 is a memory leak claim, not a destructive operation.
No outbound third-party call is added or changed; the resource/bridge branch keeps its behaviour.
No version bump, CI or deploy config; the two new env vars both have defaults so nothing is required at deploy time.
